correctness.rationale: For every finite quota-valid two-class partition matroid, equality in the average base-payment inequality forces zero payment on nonsaturated classes. When q=1, arbitrary distribution among the saturated resources is necessary and sufficient; for q>=2, base-exchange comparisons enforce uniformity within each saturated class. The finite binomial event is exact, with the threshold-overlap counted once. A binomial unimodality bound gives modular residue equidistribution at O(m^-1/2), and triangular-array CLT plus exponentially rare invalid-rank events proves the stated fixed-quota critical window. Executed independent checker: 405 full-coalition LP, 9612 exact event, 38 exact rational probability and 9 asymptotic comparisons.

value.rationale: Random availability of two complementary resource types with fixed integer quotas is a basic model of cooperative capacity/reliability. It yields a sharp observable distinction between near-certain existence of a complete production base and non-concentrating core stability. The 1/s to 1/r crossover at m^-1/2 from an arithmetic packing bottleneck is an exact natural invariant, not a chosen arbitrary finite slice; applicability is limited to iid fixed quotas, and the deterministic criterion itself is prior-covered.
